subject: Next steps: region routing & deployment mode clarifications
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@finovate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:12 -0500
Subject: Post-call recap + region & deployment questions

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the clarification items we said we'd follow up on so you have them in one thread: 

1) Primary requirement: Finovate needs all customer PII & transaction-derived prompts to stay in the EU for GDPR and local regulator review.
2) Traffic patterns: most requests will originate in EU (Dublin/Frankfurt), but some multi-region back-office jobs (~15%) run out of APAC and US processing windows.
3) Desired SLA/latency: 99.9% with p95 < 180ms for synchronous endpoints.

What we need from you to qualify next steps:
- Confirm whether the 15% cross-region batch processing can tolerate routing through an EU-resident endpoint (i.e., no strict APAC residency requirement for that workload).
- Confirm procurement timeline and whether a standard Dedicated Reserved instance or Private VPC is preferred for compliance review.

Initial recommendations (high-level):
- Hosted API (EU region) — fastest time-to-value, data residency kept in EU for synchronous traffic. Cross-region traffic from APAC/US would be routed to EU unless you require local residency for those jobs.
- Dedicated (EU reserved GPUs) — offers predictable throughput and clearer isolation; logs/audit retention configurable; good fit if procurement wants contractual capacity commitments.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) — strongest control and local-data plane; recommended if regulators insist on customer-managed network or air-gapped processing.

I'll attach the short security summary and a deployment comparison spreadsheet. Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the residency tolerance for the 15% cross-region jobs.
- If you want, schedule a short tech deep-dive with our infra engineer (Jordan) to walk through Private VPC network topology and certs.

Would next Tue or Wed afternoon CET work for the deep-dive?

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Security_Summary_v1.3.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Finovate_MATAMPLE_deployment_comparison.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@finovate.com>

Cc: Finovate Payments Procurement <procurement@finovate.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:03 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + region & deployment questions

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The synchronous customer-facing traffic must remain in the EU. No exceptions.
- The 15% batch jobs that run during our APAC window can be routed to EU as long as there is no export of raw PII fields outside the EU (we use tokenization in our pipelines; as long as tokens remain in EU, we're fine).
- Procurement asked for a cost delta between Dedicated vs Hosted (EU) and an outline of what you can contractually guarantee for data residency (is the Hosted EU offering strictly single-region data plane?).

We are leaning toward Hosted (EU) for speed but procurement will want to see the residency guarantee and a pricing delta for Dedicated.

Can you confirm Jordan's availability next Wed 16:00 CET for the tech session?

Best,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Platform Engineering, Finovate Payments

- A one-page residency statement that describes: physical region of storage/compute, cross-region telemetry visibility (control plane vs data plane), and how we handle caching/KV to ensure tokens never leave EU.
- A short pricing comparison: Hosted EU (pay-as-you-go) vs Dedicated EU (monthly reserve) including typical cost buckets (tokens, reserved GPU baseline, burst). I started a draft in the attached spreadsheet tab "Procurement_Breakdown".

I'll patch the residency statement and the procurement tab tonight. Marcus, when you talk to Olivia, reconfirm the "tokens in EU" tolerance for the batch jobs so we can put that into the statement.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + region & deployment questions

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the constraints. To confirm in writing based on our conversation and internal follow-up: 

- Redwood Hosted (EU) data plane: synchronous traffic and any stored request artifacts will remain physically in EU (we run compute and storage in the selected cloud region; logs and KV caches tied to the region).
- Cross-region batch jobs (the ~15%) can be routed to EU with tokenization enforced client-side or at ingestion — meaning raw PII is never exported outside EU in plain text. We'll include this as part of the residency statement.

Jordan is available Wed 4 Mar 16:00 CET for a 30-minute tech session (I confirmed with him). I've asked Marissa to upload the procurement cost tab and a residency statement to the shared doc. Links below.

Next steps (agreed):
- Tech deep-dive Wed 4 Mar 16:00 CET (Jordan to demo VPC diagrams and KMS options)
- Redwood to deliver a one-page residency statement + pricing delta (Hosted vs Dedicated) by EOD Fri 6 Mar
- Procurement to advise whether they need a Dedicated contract template or want to proceed with Hosted after the residency statement.

Attachments: security summary + deployment comparison. DocuSign link for standard TOU shared for procurement review: https://www.docusign.com/FP-TOU-2026

Cheers,
Marcus
